hints.title: Move-Constrained Grid Escape Obstacle
hints.text: A ball starts at (startRow, startColumn) on an m x n grid and can move up, down, left, or right up to maxMove times. How can calculating the number of ways to reach each cell at step k count all boundary escapes modulo 10^9 + 7?

hints.title: Step-Wise Boundary Escape Invariant
hints.text: Moving from cell (r, c) off any grid boundary adds the current cell path count directly to the total escapes. Moving into an adjacent in-bounds cell propagates path counts to step k + 1.

hints.title: 2D Grid Move-Stepping Procedure
hints.text: Maintain a 2D array of size m x n initialized to 0, setting (startRow, startColumn) to 1. For each move from 1 to maxMove, create a new grid. For every cell (r, c), check all 4 neighbors: if out of bounds, add current count to the answer; if in bounds, add current count to neighbor cell in new grid modulo 10^9 + 7. Swap grids and return answer modulo 10^9 + 7.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Iterates through K steps, updating each cell in constant time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recursive exploration takes O(4^K) exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Double-buffering two M x N grids uses O(M * N) memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Applying modulo arithmetic on both grid transitions and total boundary escapes.
